title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 3.

questions.question: Who was the firstborn son of David born in Hebron?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:1 states that Amnon was the firstborn son of David born in Hebron.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 3, who was the mother of Absalom?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:2 identifies Maachah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur, as the mother of Absalom.

questions.question: Which son of David was born to Eglah his wife?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:3 shows that Ithream was born to David by his wife Eglah.

questions.question: How long did David reign in Hebron according to 1 Chronicles 3?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:4 states David reigned in Hebron for seven years and six months.

questions.question: Where were Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon born?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:5 tells us these sons of David were born in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Who was the mother of Solomon and his brothers Shimea, Shobab, and Nathan?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:5 identifies Bathshua, daughter of Ammiel, as their mother.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT listed among David's sons born in Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:6 and 3:8 list Ibhar, Elishama, and Eliphelet as sons born in Jerusalem; Abital was mother of Shephatiah born in Hebron (3:3).

questions.question: How many sons of David born in Jerusalem are named in 1 Chronicles 3:6-8?
questions.explanation: Verses 6 through 8 name Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet, totaling thirteen sons born in Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Tamar was one of David's sons mentioned in 1 Chronicles 3.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:9 refers to Tamar as David's sister, not as one of his sons.

questions.question: True or False: David reigned in Jerusalem for thirty-three years.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:4 states David reigned thirty-three years in Jerusalem.

questions.question: Which son of David was born to Ahinoam the Jezreelitess?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:1 identifies Amnon as the son of David by Ahinoam the Jezreelitess.

questions.question: Who was the fourth son of David born in Hebron?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:2 lists Adonijah as the fourth son born in Hebron.

questions.question: True or False: Nathan was one of David's sons born in Hebron.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:5 shows Nathan was born in Jerusalem, not Hebron.

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 3, which son of David born in Jerusalem is mentioned first?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:5 lists Shimea first among the sons born in Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Shephatiah was born to Abital.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:3 states Shephatiah was born to Abital.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 3:9, who were mentioned alongside the sons of David?
options: The sons of the concubines and Tamar their sister
The sons of Solomon and Rehoboam
The sons of Jehoiakim and Zedekiah
The sons of Josiah and Shallum
questions.correctAnswer: The sons of the concubines and Tamar their sister
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:9 explicitly states that besides the sons of David, there were the sons of the concubines and Tamar their sister. This highlights the full family context of David's lineage.

questions.question: What can we learn about faithfulness in leadership from the sequence of kings listed in 1 Chronicles 3:10-14?
options: Leadership is passed down through a God-ordained lineage showing continuity and responsibility
Only the strongest king retains the throne regardless of lineage
Kingship is unrelated to family ties and depends solely on military power
Faithfulness is irrelevant as long as the king is popular
questions.correctAnswer: Leadership is passed down through a God-ordained lineage showing continuity and responsibility
questions.explanation: Verses 10-14 list the descendants of Solomon, emphasizing the importance of generational faithfulness and responsibility in leadership, reflecting God's providence and covenant with David's line.

questions.question: Who was the firstborn son of Josiah according to 1 Chronicles 3:15?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:15 clearly names Johanan as the firstborn son of Josiah, followed by Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Shallum.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue can be drawn from understanding the long genealogy listed in 1 Chronicles 3:10-16?
options: Humility, recognizing that we are part of a larger story and legacy
questions.correctAnswer: Humility, recognizing that we are part of a larger story and legacy
questions.explanation: The genealogy reminds believers of their place in God's unfolding plan, teaching humility and the importance of honoring the legacy and faithfulness of those who came before, as seen in verses 10-16.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 3:16, Zedekiah was a son of Jehoiakim.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:16 explicitly states that the sons of Jehoiakim were Jeconiah and Zedekiah, confirming Zedekiah as his son.

questions.question: Based on 1 Chronicles 3:10-14, how does the passage teach us about the importance of legacy in Christian living?
options: It shows that godly legacy influences future generations and calls for faithfulness
It suggests legacy is unimportant and can be ignored
It emphasizes only personal success matters
It teaches that only the firstborn should be respected
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that godly legacy influences future generations and calls for faithfulness
questions.explanation: The detailed lineage from Solomon to Josiah teaches that faithfulness and obedience to God affect not just individuals but generations, encouraging believers to live responsibly for their legacy (verses 10-14).

questions.question: Who was Jeconiah's son as recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:17?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:17 identifies Salathiel as the son of Jeconiah, with Assir also mentioned but without direct paternal relation specified.

questions.question: What does the listing of many descendants in 1 Chronicles 3:18-24 teach about the value of family and perseverance?
options: It highlights God's sustaining of a family line through trials and the importance of perseverance
It indicates that family size guarantees success
It suggests only the firstborn are important
It implies family connections are irrelevant
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights God's sustaining of a family line through trials and the importance of perseverance
questions.explanation: The extensive genealogy shows God's faithfulness through many generations despite challenges, encouraging believers to persevere and value family as part of God's plan (verses 18-24).

questions.question: In 1 Chronicles 3:15-16, what does the relationship between Josiah, Jehoiakim, and Zedekiah teach about God's providence?
options: God maintains authority over the lineage of kings, even through difficult times
Kingship is purely political without divine involvement
God favors only the firstborn son
Providence does not affect human leadership
questions.correctAnswer: God maintains authority over the lineage of kings, even through difficult times
questions.explanation: The genealogical record reveals God's sovereign control over the royal line, sustaining it through various kings, demonstrating divine providence despite historical challenges (verses 15-16).

questions.question: True or False: Tamar was one of the sons of David according to 1 Chronicles 3:9.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:9 clearly distinguishes Tamar as the sister of David's sons, not one of the sons, making the statement false.

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 3:10-14 illustrate the importance of prayer and obedience in leadership?
options: By showing a godly lineage where obedience to God was crucial for their reigns
By focusing only on military conquest
By ignoring spiritual matters in favor of politics
By emphasizing wealth as the key to leadership
questions.correctAnswer: By showing a godly lineage where obedience to God was crucial for their reigns
questions.explanation: The passage lists kings known for their faith or disobedience, teaching that prayerful obedience to God is foundational for successful leadership (verses 10-14).

questions.question: Who are the four sons of Bathshua mentioned in 1 Chronicles 3:5?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:5 lists these four sons of David born in Jerusalem by Bathshua, highlighting the family lineage in the city.

questions.question: What does the genealogy in 1 Chronicles 3:17-19 demonstrate about God’s faithfulness in times of exile and hardship?
options: God preserves His people and their heritage even in difficult circumstances
God abandons His people during exile
questions.correctAnswer: God preserves His people and their heritage even in difficult circumstances
questions.explanation: The listing of descendants like Zerubbabel during exile shows God’s ongoing care and preservation of His covenant people and their lineage despite adversity (verses 17-19).

questions.question: True or False: 1 Chronicles 3:22 lists exactly six sons of Shemaiah.
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 3:22, Shemaiah had six sons: Hattush, Igeal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat, confirming the correct number is six.

questions.question: How does the detailed listing of descendants in 1 Chronicles 3:20-24 encourage believers struggling with identity and purpose?
options: It shows that every individual is part of God's larger plan and has a meaningful role
It suggests only leaders have importance
It implies that numbers matter more than character
It teaches that identity is fixed solely by birthright
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that every individual is part of God's larger plan and has a meaningful role
questions.explanation: The extensive genealogies highlight God's inclusion of many individuals in His plan, encouraging believers to see their unique value and purpose regardless of status (verses 20-24).

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 3.

questions.question: Who was the son of Jeconiah mentioned as the father of Salathiel?
questions.explanation: Verse 1 Chronicles 3:17 states that Assir is the son of Jeconiah and Salathiel is his son, making Assir the direct father of Salathiel.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed as a son of Jeconiah in 1 Chronicles 3?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:17-18 lists Assir, Salathiel, and Malchiram as sons of Jeconiah, but Zerubbabel is actually a son of Pedaiah, not Jeconiah himself, as shown in verse 19.

questions.question: Who was the father of Zerubbabel according to 1 Chronicles 3?
questions.explanation: Verse 19 clearly states that Zerubbabel was a son of Pedaiah, distinguishing him from Jeconiah’s direct sons.

questions.question: Which sister is mentioned among the sons of Zerubbabel in 1 Chronicles 3?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:19 records Shelomith as the sister of Meshullam and Hananiah, sons of Zerubbabel.

questions.question: How many sons of Zerubbabel are named in 1 Chronicles 3:20?
questions.explanation: Verse 20 lists five sons of Zerubbabel: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushabhesed.

questions.question: Which name is NOT listed as a son of Hananiah in this chapter?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:21 states that Hananiah's sons were Pelatiah and Jesaiah, while Shemaiah was a son of Shechaniah mentioned in verse 22.

questions.question: What is the relationship between Shemaiah and Hattush according to 1 Chronicles 3?
questions.explanation: Verse 22 explains that Shemaiah had sons including Hattush, meaning Shemaiah is Hattush’s father.

questions.question: How many sons of Neariah are named in 1 Chronicles 3?
questions.explanation: Verse 23 lists three sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam.

questions.question: Which literary device is most evident in the genealogical lists of 1 Chronicles 3, especially from verses 17 to 24?
questions.explanation: The chapter opens and closes with genealogies, creating an inclusio that frames the Davidic line and emphasizes continuity, as seen in verses 17 and 24.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew name 'Zerubbabel' which appears in 1 Chronicles 3?
questions.explanation: The name Zerubbabel means 'seed (offspring) of Babylon,' reflecting his birth during the Babylonian exile, as supported by historical context in verse 19.

questions.question: Which king's sons are listed immediately before the genealogy of Jeconiah and his descendants in 1 Chronicles 3?
questions.explanation: Verse 15 lists the sons of Josiah, just before the genealogy of Jehoiakim, Jeconiah, and their descendants in verses 16 and following.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the Davidic lineage and thus connects to 1 Chronicles 3 genealogy?
questions.explanation: Matthew 1:1-17 traces Jesus’ genealogy through David and Jeconiah, directly connecting and fulfilling the lineage listed in 1 Chronicles 3.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 3, Solomon's son was Rehoboam, who is an ancestor of Zerubbabel.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:10-19 shows the lineage from Solomon to Rehoboam and onward to Zerubbabel, establishing Rehoboam as an ancestor of Zerubbabel.

questions.question: True or False: The chapter lists Tamar as one of David's sons.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 3:9 mentions Tamar as David's sister, not as a son, therefore the statement is false.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage prophesies the restoration of the Davidic line, which is exemplified by the genealogy in 1 Chronicles 3?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 33:17 prophesies that David will always have a descendant to sit on the throne, which is fulfilled by the detailed genealogy in 1 Chronicles 3.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: Which doctrine is illustrated by the detailed genealogy of David's descendants in 1 Chronicles 3:10-14?
options: Doctrine of Election and Covenant Faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of Election and Covenant Faithfulness
questions.explanation: The genealogy from Solomon to Josiah (1 Chronicles 3:10-14) shows God's covenant faithfulness in preserving David's line despite human failures, illustrating the doctrine of election and covenant faithfulness (cf. Romans 11:2-5).

questions.question: What does the mention of Bathshua as the mother of four of David's sons in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:5) reveal about God's providence?
options: Providence in the establishment of the Davidic line
Providence in Israel's conquest of Canaan
Providence in the giving of the Law
Providence in the building of the Temple
questions.correctAnswer: Providence in the establishment of the Davidic line
questions.explanation: Bathshua's bearing of Solomon and other sons in Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:5) highlights God's providential care in establishing the Davidic dynasty, which is central to messianic fulfillment (2 Samuel 7:12-16).

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 3:4 demonstrate God's attribute of sovereignty?
options: God sovereignly appointed David's reign length in Hebron and Jerusalem
God's sovereignty limited by human free will
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly appointed David's reign length in Hebron and Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states David reigned seven years and six months in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem, showing God's sovereign control over the timing and duration of David's kingship (cf. Psalm 75:6-7).

questions.question: What theological significance does the inclusion of Tamar alongside David's sons in 1 Chronicles 3:9 have?
options: It acknowledges the impact of familial sin and God's mercy
It highlights the role of women prophets
It indicates Tamar was a royal ruler
questions.correctAnswer: It acknowledges the impact of familial sin and God's mercy
questions.explanation: Mentioning Tamar, David's daughter involved in a tragic family incident (2 Samuel 13), alongside his sons reflects the reality of sin within God's covenant people and His ongoing mercy (1 Chronicles 3:9).

questions.question: What does the listing of Zerubbabel and his descendants in 1 Chronicles 3:19-20 teach about God's redemptive plan?
options: God’s faithfulness in preserving the messianic line through exile
God’s rejection of the Davidic line
God’s establishment of a new priesthood
God’s promise of universal salvation regardless of lineage
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness in preserving the messianic line through exile
questions.explanation: Zerubbabel, a key post-exilic leader and descendant of David, shows God's preservation of the messianic line despite exile, underscoring divine faithfulness to redemptive promises (1 Chronicles 3:19-20; cf. Ezra 3:2).

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 3:16, who were the sons of Jehoiakim, and what does their mention indicate about God's providence?
options: Jeconiah and Zedekiah; God's providence in continuing the royal line despite Judah's exile
Rehoboam and Abijah; God's providence in establishing the kingdom
Nathan and Solomon; God's providence in the Davidic covenant
Amon and Josiah; God's providence in temple restoration
questions.correctAnswer: Jeconiah and Zedekiah; God's providence in continuing the royal line despite Judah's exile
questions.explanation: Jehoiakim’s sons, Jeconiah and Zedekiah, represent the continuation of David’s line during a time of political collapse, showing God's providence even amid judgment (1 Chronicles 3:16).

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about God's covenant faithfulness can be drawn from 1 Chronicles 3:1-3 and 3:10-14?
options: God faithfully preserves the Davidic line through all generations despite human sin
God’s covenant is conditional on perfect obedience
God prioritizes the Levitical priesthood over the royal line
God’s promises are limited to the firstborn sons
questions.correctAnswer: God faithfully preserves the Davidic line through all generations despite human sin
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 list David’s sons born in Hebron, and 10-14 trace Solomon’s descendants, showing God’s covenant faithfulness in maintaining David’s royal line across generations despite their failings (1 Chronicles 3:1-3, 10-14).

questions.question: How does 1 Chronicles 3:17-18 contribute to our understanding of God's providence in history?
options: By listing Jeconiah’s sons, it demonstrates God’s care in preserving the royal lineage during exile
By showing God’s rejection of the Davidic covenant
questions.correctAnswer: By listing Jeconiah’s sons, it demonstrates God’s care in preserving the royal lineage during exile
questions.explanation: Listing Jeconiah’s sons in exile times shows God’s providential preservation of the covenant line even in adverse conditions (1 Chronicles 3:17-18; cf. Jeremiah 22:24-30).

questions.question: What attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated by the succession of kings from Solomon to Josiah as recorded in 1 Chronicles 3:10-14?
questions.explanation: The uninterrupted succession from Solomon through Josiah (1 Chronicles 3:10-14) highlights God’s faithfulness to His covenant promises made to David (cf. 2 Samuel 7:16).

questions.question: From the genealogy in 1 Chronicles 3:19-24, what theological truth about God's sustaining grace can be inferred?
options: God sustains His people through successive generations even after exile
God’s grace is limited to the first generation
God’s grace is only for priests
God’s grace is conditional on geographical location
questions.correctAnswer: God sustains His people through successive generations even after exile
questions.explanation: The detailed lineage from Zerubbabel through Elioenai and his sons (1 Chronicles 3:19-24) shows God’s sustaining grace preserving His people and promises through generations despite hardships like exile.

questions.question: Sceptics claim genealogies are irrelevant to understanding God's plan. What does 1 Chronicles 3:10-24 teach about the importance of genealogies in biblical theology?
options: Genealogies demonstrate God's unfolding plan of redemption through history
Genealogies are merely cultural artifacts with no theological value
Genealogies are symbolic with no historical basis
questions.correctAnswer: Genealogies demonstrate God's unfolding plan of redemption through history
questions.explanation: This genealogy in 1 Chronicles 3:10-24 reveals the historical unfolding of God's covenant promises, especially regarding the Davidic line leading to the Messiah (cf. Matthew 1:1-17).

questions.question: What combined teaching about human sin and divine grace can be drawn from 1 Chronicles 3:2 and 3:15?
options: Despite human failings in David's family, God's covenant promises continue
Sin nullifies God's promises to David's descendants
Only the sons from David's first wife are blessed
Women have no role in God's covenant
questions.correctAnswer: Despite human failings in David's family, God's covenant promises continue
questions.explanation: Verses 2 and 15 mention sons born from various wives, including Adonijah and the sons of Josiah, illustrating that despite human sin and complex family dynamics, God's covenant with David's line endures (1 Chronicles 3:2, 15).

questions.question: How does the reference to the reign of David in Hebron and Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4) contribute to the narrative arc of the Davidic covenant in Scripture?
options: It marks the historical and theological establishment of the Davidic dynasty
It emphasizes Saul’s kingship over Israel
It focuses on the Levitical priesthood
questions.correctAnswer: It marks the historical and theological establishment of the Davidic dynasty
questions.explanation: David’s reign in Hebron and Jerusalem (1 Chronicles 3:4) is foundational historically and theologically for the Davidic covenant, which is central to the messianic promises in Scripture (cf. 2 Samuel 7).

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about Christ is foreshadowed by the lineage beginning with David’s sons in 1 Chronicles 3:1-9 and culminating in Solomon’s descendants in verses 10-14?
options: The Messianic prophecy of Christ’s Davidic descent
questions.correctAnswer: The Messianic prophecy of Christ’s Davidic descent
questions.explanation: The genealogy from David’s sons through Solomon to later kings (1 Chronicles 3:1-14) directly foreshadows Christ’s Messiahship as the promised descendant of David (cf. Luke 3:23-31).

questions.question: What theological insight is gained by comparing the sons of Shechaniah and Shemaiah in 1 Chronicles 3:22 with the sons of Elioenai in 3:23-24?
options: God’s faithfulness in preserving the covenant community through post-exilic generations
God’s judgment ending the Davidic line
God’s selection of only priests for leadership
God’s rejection of lineage in favor of spiritual gifts
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness in preserving the covenant community through post-exilic generations
questions.explanation: The genealogies in 3:22-24 document post-exilic descendants, demonstrating God's faithfulness in sustaining His covenant people through difficult historical transitions.
